label: Chapter 1
title: Modules, packages, first simulation
summary: Set up a Go module and write an epsilon-greedy bandit simulation that prints its regret.

label: Chapter 2
title: Interfaces and methods
summary: Introduce the Policy interface, add UCB1, and swap policies without touching the runner.

label: Chapter 3
title: Errors, tests, benchmarks
summary: Make failure explicit with error values, then pin behaviour down with table-driven tests, golden files and benchmarks.

label: Chapter 4
title: Generics and the comparison harness
summary: Add Thompson sampling, write generic helpers where they earn their place, and chart regret across many seeds.

label: Chapter 5
title: Goroutines and channels
summary: Run simulations in parallel with fan-out and fan-in.

label: Chapter 6
title: Shared state
summary: Mutexes, atomics and the race detector: see a real race, then fix it.

label: Chapter 7
title: Context, select, worker pools
summary: Cancellation, timeouts and bounded worker pools without goroutine leaks.

label: Chapter 8
title: net/http
summary: Serve select and reward endpoints with JSON, middleware and httptest.

label: Chapter 9
title: Structure and operations
summary: Project layout, configuration, structured logging and graceful shutdown.

label: Chapter 10
title: Persistence and delayed feedback
summary: Store bandit state and pending selections; handle rewards that arrive late or never.

label: Chapter 11
title: Observability and performance
summary: Prometheus metrics, pprof, a load generator and one real bottleneck.

label: Chapter 12
title: Why naive replicas break the bandit
summary: Watch replicas diverge, then fix it with mergeable counts and measure the cost of staleness.

label: Chapter 13
title: Splitting into services
summary: Protobuf and gRPC: a policy service, feedback ingest and an aggregator.

label: Chapter 14
title: Running the system
summary: Docker, Compose, load balancing, and a Python client for the Go service.

label: Capstone
title: End-to-end load test
summary: Compare policies across replicas with staleness, and decide where to go next.
